sources.facts: Measured 5.20 m near-cube, east and south entrances, pointed dome above pendentives, locator and raised black inscription over the main entrance.
Shaukat Mahmood’s architectural field research distinguishes the small Baba Farid tomb from the larger adjacent Ala-ud-Din mausoleum and describes the chamber and dome.
The district register names the east Nuri Darwaza and the south Bahishti Darwaza.
The caretaker agency describes the chamber as white marble. Archaeology survey and district record agree on the south opening.
The 1914–15 survey catalogue identifies the south face as the Bahishti doorway facade. Archive metadata only.
The national intangible heritage register records that the Bahishti Darwaza opens during the Urs.
Ahmad Nabi Khan’s architectural study describes the pendentive system, cusped dome and prominent long pinnacle. Written description only.

architecture.roof: cusped dome on pendentives with a long pinnacle
